question.text: A wire, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> in length and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> in diameter at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is kept in low temperature at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>170</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and is stretched by hanging a weight of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> at one end. The change in length of the wire is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>[</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></msup></math> <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>ms</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>]</mo></math>

solution.text:
The change in length of the wire due to change in temperature

=αLT=1.2×10-5×3×-170-30

=-7.2×10-3m

The change in the length of the wire due to the stretching force

=F LA Y= 10×10×30.75×10-6×2×1011

=2×10-3 m

The total change in the length of the wire

=-7.2×10-3+2×10-3

=-5.2×10-3 m=-5.2 mm

The negative sign indicates contraction of the wire
